full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 11 of 2017 against the petitioners as defendant for a decree of permanent injunction restraining the defendants from obstructing the plaintiff from using the pathway measuring 53'.6" fit x 12'.6" running from east to west, stating that the property originally belonged to one Sheikh Anwar Ali who purchased the same from one Sri Showmendra Mohan by sale deed No. 1209 dated 13-2-1952. The said Sheikh Anwar Ali died leaving his wife Jebunnesa Begum and son Sheikh Golam Rahman. The said Golam Rahman and Jebunnesa by 4 (four) separate sale deeds dated 28-6-1974 transferred the property measuring 0750 sataks to the plaintiffs and 0750 sataks to defendant Nos. 1 and 2. In the deeds of the defendants there has been a covenant that the plaintiffs shall have right of pathway over the north side of the property transferred to the defendants measuring 53'6" x 8' ft and the said property is not transferable by the defendants to anybody. 

 3. Accordingly, the plaintiffs have been enjoying the said road as mentioned in the sale deeds of both the parties. Subsequently, by two separate deeds dated 24-1-1987 both plaintiffs and defendants again purchased 0.0055 sataks of land each from Golam Rahman and her mother. The plaintiffs claimed that the property purchased by the defendants on 24-1-1987 measuring 0.0055 sataks is situated north side of the existing road and it was purchased for the purpose of widening the existing road. But the defendants in violation of the terms as contained in their sale deeds dated 28-6-1974 most illegally entered into an agreement with the developer, defendant No. 5 Ambit Builders Ltd. for construction of a multistoried building for the entire property purchased by them including the land on which the pathway is existing and the developer after entering into the agreement for development of the property obtained sanction and approval of the building plan from RAJUK showing the entire land measuring 0.804 sataks without excluding the land of the pathway. After obtaining sanction from RAJUK the developer defendant No. 5 started construction of the building encroaching the existing road and obstructing the plaintiffs from using the said road specifically prescribed for them. 

 4. The plaintiffs raised objection and requested the defendants not to encroach the road and obstruct smooth enjoyment of the road in question but they did not pay any heed to their requests. Consequently, the plaintiffs filed the instant suit for a decree of permanent injunction against the defendants not to obstruct or create any hindrance or disturbances in smooth enjoyment of the road in question. In the suit the plaintiffs filed an application under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure ("CPC") praying for temporary injunction against the defendants. The trial court issued notice to show cause to the defendants who appeared in suit and filed written objection. The trial court though heard the application for injunction but disposed of the same by a short order directing both the parties to the suit to maintain status quo in respect of the suit pathway. 

 5. The defendants being aggrieved filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 170 of 2017 wherein they filed an application for stay operation of the order passed by the trial court. The lower appellate court stayed the order of status quo passed by the trial court. Against the said order the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No. 112 of 2018 before this Court and prayed for stay. This Court issued Rule and stayed operation of the order passed by the lower appellate court. Against the said order the defendants moved before the Appellate Division. Appellate Division kept the appeal stand over for one week and directed the appellant petitioners to get the matter heard before the High Court Division. During pendency of the civil revision, the appeal was heard and disposed of by the lower appellate court and disallowed the appeal maintaining order of status quo passed by the trial court by the impugned judgment and order. 

 7. The plaintiff opposite parties entered into appearance and contested the Rule by filing counter affidavit contending, inter alia, that since 1974 the plaintiffs uninterruptedly without any disturbance from any quarter using and enjoying the suit pathway measuring 53'.6" x 8' ft. Thereafter, for widening the said pathway the defendants by a deed dated 24-1-1987 again purchased 0.0055 sataks of land from original owners which is situated just north side of the existing pathway measuring 53'6" x 4'6" ft. The plaintiffs in addition to the existing 8' ft road along with subseqiuently purchased 4½' ft land measuring 12½' ft width have been using as their pathway till today. The defendants in violation of terms and conditions as contained in their deeds dated 20-8-1974 most unfortunately entered into an agreement with the developer, the defendant No. 5 for development of the property by constructing multi-storied building without excluding the property prescribed for pathway of the plaintiffs. And the developer obtained building plan showing the entire land as land of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 which they cannot do as per their deeds as well as existing condition of the suit property. It is also stated that the defendant No. 5 by using their force trying to encroach the existing road under which all the facilities such as WASA, Telephone and Gas line have been installed and, as such, they prayed for an order of injunction. Both the courts below considering the facts and circumstances as well as balance of convenience and finding prima facie case in favour of the plaintiffs granted an order of status quo directing both the parties which in fact caused no harm and or injustice to the parties to the suit. 

 8. Mr AFM Mezbah Uddin, Senior Advocate with Mr Oziullah and Mr Kamal Hossain, Advocates appearing for the petitioners submit that admittedly the disputed property along with non-suited property belong to present petitioners who purchased the same in the year 1974. But there is a condition in the purchase deed that the plaintiffs will have the right of use of the pathway running from east to west measuring 53'6" x 8' ft just north side of the petitioners' property. Accordingly as per sale deed 53'6" x 8' ft road is now existing and the plaintiffs are using the same. He further submits that there is no dispute about the pathway described in the deeds of the parties. But subsequently on 24-1-1997 by deed No. 358 the petitioners purchased 0055 sataks of land from the original owner Golam Rahman and others. The said property is the adjacent property of the petitioners and it is not part and parcel of the existing pathway at all. But the plaintiffs taking advantage of existing pathway as mentioned in the deeds of the year 1974 tried to claim that the property purchased in the year 1987 by the petitioners was for the purpose of widening the road for their use. It is absolute unbelievable and beyond the probability that the petitioners by their own money purchased the land for the benefit and use of the plaintiffs who already got a pathway on the property of the petitioners. He further goes to submits that the plaintiffs never raised any dispute regarding width of the pathway of the plaintiffs but while the plaintiff entered into agreement for development of the property with the defendant No. 5, developer the plaintiffs with a view to harass the petitioners and create disturbance most unfortunately raised a claim that the property purchased by the petitioners in the year 1987 is part of the pathway and the plaintiffs have been using the same as integral part of the existing road and on that claim they filed the present suit for injunction though in the cause title it has been described that the suit is for declaration and injunction. He further argued that a suit for injunction claiming easement right is not maintainable without prayer for a declaration of that right. It is also submitted that the trial court in its impugned order discussed no case of the parties and without disposing the application on merit passed the impugned order merely saying "both the parties are directed to maintain status quo in respect of the pathway". The appellate court also without going through the present position of the suit land and appreciating the case of the petitioners disallowed the appeal affirming the order passed by the trial court. 

 9. It is argued that in disposing an application for injunction the courts below ought to have framed issues to the effect that whether the plaintiffs have a good prima facie case, balance of conveniences and whether in the event of refusing injunction the plaintiffs shall suffer irreparable loss. Both the courts below in passing the impugned orders did not follow the principles enunciated for granting injunction. As such, the order under challenged is liable to be set-aside. 

 10. Mr Nurul Amin, learned Senior Advocate with Mr Md Ramzan Ali Sikder, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party submits that, this is a case relating to pathway of the plaintiffs. Both the parties admit that there is a pathway as mentioned in the deed of the petitioner-defendants. It is not the case of the parties that the plaintiffs are not using the pathway since their purchase in the year 1974. Mr Nurul Amin further submits that the sale deed of the petitioners clearly shows that a pathway measuring 53'.6" x 8' ft kept open just northern side of the petitioners' land for use of the plaintiffs. Subsequently, for widening of the pathway of the plaintiffs, as well as the defendants both the parties by two separate sale deeds dated 24-1-1997 purchased 0055 sataks land each from the original owner and the said property situated just northern side of the existing road. As per deed of the petitioners the plaintiffs-opposite parties are entitled to use and enjoy the pathway and the petitioners are entitled to construct building on the land excluding the land prescribed for the road. But the present petitioners in violation of the terms and conditions of the sale deed of the year 1974 entered into an agreement with the defendant No. 5 developer for the entire property covered by the sale deeds of the year 1974 and 1987 which they cannot do. 

 11. He further submits that taking advantage of giving entire property to the developer by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 the defendant No. 5 obtained a building plan on the property showing entire land to be the land of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 but in fact after exclusion of the property covered by the pathway the defendants are entitled to get sanction or approval of building plan only on 0.0654 sataks of land not on the land measuring 0.804 sataks. It is also argued that had the defendants given the property to the developer excluding the land of the existing pathway there would not have arisen any dispute regarding pathway of the plaintiffs. He further goes to submits that the defendant No. 5, developer obtained building plan from RAJUK on the property beyond entitlement of the defendants. If the developer is allowed to continue with the construction work and to build the building, violating the Rules in this regard, the pathway of the plaintiffs will be absolutely obstructed and, as such, to prevent abuse of the process of the court and multiplicity of suits the trial court considering facts and circumstances of the case granted an order of status quo directing both the parties which in no manner caused injustice to anybody including the defendants. The appellate court maintained the order of the trial court by disposing the application on merit holding that the defendants admitted existence of a pathway to be enjoyed and used by the plaintiffs and, as such, defendants ought to have excluded the said property from their agreement entered with the defendant No. 5. As such, both the courts below rightly passed the order directing the parties to maintain status quo. In support of his submissions he has referred to the case of Sikam Fashion Ltd. vs Miaco Ltd. reported in 10 BLT (AD) 39 (para 4). 

 13. In the present suit both the parties admitted that the plaintiffs got a pathway over the property purchased by the defendants in suit. The pathway is admittedly measuring 53'.6" x 8' ft. running from east to west. Further case of the plaintiff is that the defendants by a sale deed dated 24-1-1987 purchased 0055 sataks land from the same plot situated in the north of the existing pathway and the defendants are trying to build the proposed building by encroaching the said strip of land which is the part and parcel of the existing pathway of the plaintiffs. By a sketch map the plaintiff-opposite party tried to impress upon the court that the property purchased by the defendants in the year 1987 is situated just adjacent north to the existing road and not adjacent to the land of the defendants as per boundary given in the deed of the year 1987 and, as such, the defendant cannot extend proposed building by encroaching over the existing road. On the other hand the petitioner-defendants submit that the property purchased in the year 1987 is the property situated just adjacent north to the defendants present land and adjacent south to the existing pathway and the property in question was never purchased for widening the pathway. It is also claimed that the sale deed of the year 1987 does not say and disclose any such condition that the property purchased for the widening of the road like the sale deed of the year 1974. 

 14. Had it been purchased for the purpose of widening the road there must have been a condition in the sale deed like the deed of the year 1974. It is also claimed that it is unusual that the defendants on their own initiative and with their own money purchased some quantum of land for the benefit of the plaintiffs instead of purchasing the same by the plaintiffs. From the papers and documents available in record this Court finds that there is no dispute regarding a pathway measuring 53'.6" x 8' ft but the dispute is whether the property purchased by the defendants on 24-1-1987 is the adjacent land to the north of the plaintiffs pathway and whether the property measuring 53'.6" x 4½' is lying just north side of the existing road as claimed by the plaintiffs. In this situation unless the position of the property is inspected or investigated physically by an Advocate Commissioner appointed by the court and obtained report thereof it cannot be said that the present existing road is measuring 12' ft or 8' ft width. 

 15. Both the courts below while disposing the application for injunction failed to ascertain present position of the suit pathway and to consider the admission made by the plaintiffs in last part of paragraph No. 11 of the plaint in suit to the effect that the plaintiffs have already been dispossessed from 21' x 3' width land in question much before filing of the suit. Moreover, from the annxures 3 and 4 annexed to the counter affidavit, the agreement entered in between the developer defendant No. 5 and irrevocable power of attorney executed by the defendants empowering the defendant No. 5 show that the defendants executed the said agreement and power of attorney for entire property covered by deeds dated 28-6-1974 and 24-1-1987 without excluding the property covered by pathway and showing existence of the pathway in question which led both the courts below to find that the defendants in violation of the terms of the sale deed executed the agreement with the developer for the entire property which they cannot do and considering such aspect the appellate court in the impugned order has observed that the defendants ignoring the existence of the pathway and excluding the property covered by it executed the agreement for entire property which compelled the plaintiffs filing of the present suit and found an arguable case in favour of the plaintiffs. This court finds that there is a dispute between the parties regarding present position of the existing road and its measurement. I think that the length and width of the existing road and its position is required to be ascertained first and without ascertaining the present position of the disputed pathway, effective disposal of the application for injunction as well as the suit could not be done.
